title: Caitlin Clark tabbed for shocking next move by Fever head coach Stephanie White - NewsBreak
text:
By Jarrod Castillo ,
1 hours ago Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White outlined what the next step is in Caitlin Clark's development By Reach Publishing Services Limited LOS ANGELES — Caitlin Clark could have a new aspect of her game develop in the near future.
Since her college days, Clark has captivated fans with her incredible shooting range, hitting 3-pointers from more than 24 feet with ease. The Indiana Fever star has shown impressive vision as the primary ball handler, finding her teammates at the right time as she dumps off the ball.
Now, head coach Stephanie White has outlined where the star needs to improve as she continues to grow in the league, putting to bed any concerns about her play .
• Scottie Scheffler says he 'doesn't need' Rory McIlroy at PGA Championship
• Rory McIlroy brutally mocked future PGA Championship venue leaving reporters in stitches
"I think she has a lot of room for growth," White said to reporters when asked by Mirror U.S. Sports where she envisions Clark growing in seasons to come. "Really managing the game. Managing where we get her teammates on the floor and how we get them looks. Managing the way to manipulate the defense to get what you want."
What's more, White has been impressed with Clark's ability to get to the rim and believes the sky is the limit for the Fever star, so long as she continues to work on her game. That includes having her be a presence in the paint.
"I keep telling her that we're going to add a post-up game too because she's got really great size and she's got great touch around the rim," White continued. "She can add that, and being a facilitator from that position on the floor is another area."
Of note, during the 2024 season, in which Clark played all 40 games, she shot 62.3 percent from 0-3 feet, while from 3-10 feet, that number is 47.2 percent.
Along with potentially adding a post-up game, White noted that the Fever are hoping to expand where she operates on the floor.
"The biggest thing we're challenging her on this year is to play in line to in line across the floor," the head coach noted. "In college, it was mostly lane line to lane line.
"Last year, we wanted this to be free throw line extended to free throw line extended, so we really want to move her around the floor a lot more, and we want to try to ease up the burden that she has bringing the ball down the floor 94 feet against pressure all game long."
• Angel Reese does what Caitlin Clark couldn't against Paige Bueckers
• 'Ragebait' Caitlin Clark view sparks debate among WNBA fans
For now, it remains to be seen how Clark will respond to potentially developing a post-game while also being relieved of the pressure she often faces as one of the Fever's primary ball handlers.
It must be noted that, to start the season, Clark has been dealing with a back issue, with the star spotted wearing a heating pack on her back in Indiana's first game and during breaks in the action against the Sparks.
By design, playing in the post leads to a more physical brand of basketball, and so long as the star's coaching staff understands her capabilities, it could be to her advantage.
The Fever will return to Indiana for their next game while the Sparks welcome the Toronto Tempo on Friday.
